status: corrected during internal audit before bundle3 commit

corrections.issue: W initially replaced strict proof sets with whole-document fields, discarding strict facts when W's reviewed subset did not repeat them.
corrections.change: W now unions strict evidence with additional reviewed parts of the same reached document. The transition graph and click cost remain fixed.
corrections.counterexample: C4-6 strict wait_all and ten Python second-hop rows had facts missing in their narrower reviewed W metadata.
corrections.verification: Every W evidence set and complete-ID set must contain its strict counterpart. Missing fragments and failed arrivals remain failures.

corrections.issue: Destination normalization initially omitted version_alignment, allowing subconditions from Python3.15.2 or a pre-release proposal to combine with another source's3.11 availability.
corrections.change: For C3/C4 arithmetic, admit only actual /3.11/ manuals, PEP654 Final, or the explicit PEP6543.11 acceptance announcement. Other documents keep their observed facts, but context-mismatched or unknown-version facts do not enter the3.11 proof union.
corrections.counterexample: The actual /3/ exceptions, compound and tutorial links resolve to observed3.15.2; historical discussion and an initial implementation are not automatically final3.11 contracts.
corrections.verification: The known PEP entry→Specification path remains valid. Inspect excluded version-mismatched records in evidence/pandoc/control-second-hop-coding.json.

corrections.issue: The transport harness only checks raw href occurrence in the whole newly fetched DOM. A changed source might move that href outside its frozen strict window; redirects might alter relative resolution.
corrections.change: Scoring now admits a second-hop proof only if the first successful response matches its frozen byte SHA and urljoin(actual final source URL, raw href) equals the planned destination. Otherwise retain observed HTTP/fragment destination but exclude it from strict-path proof.
corrections.verification: Fixed source SHA makes the sealed strict-window occurrence auditable. This does not silently broaden the source window or repair a redirected path.
